items.summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A wide binary star takes thousands of years to complete one orbit, so its eccentricity usually cannot be found by following the orbit. Astronomers instead use the angle Γ between the pair's projected separation and projected relative velocity, whose distribution over many binaries depends on the population's eccentricity law. Hwang, Ting and Zakamska (MNRAS 2022, Appendix B) asked whether this angle distribution determines the eccentricity distribution uniquely. In the ideal model (random orbital phase, uniformly random 3D orientation, error-free projections) this package derives the likelihood of one angle in closed form, p(γ|e) = [acosh(1/e) − 1{|cos γ| > e} acosh(|cos γ|/e)] / (π sin²γ), and shows that its mixtures are classical Abel transforms. This gives an explicit inverse for every eccentricity law, including atoms: different eccentricity laws never give the same angle law. The inverse is continuous in the weak topology but discontinuous in total variation, so fine structure can be nearly invisible. Moments need no inversion: E√(1−e²) = (π/2) E sin³Γ and E e² = 1/2 + E cos 2Γ − (1/2) E cos 4Γ; these are the only symmetric unbiased single-angle observables for their targets and give near-efficient power-law index estimators. Two exact selection results bear on Gaia samples: thermal populations keep a uniform angle law under selections that ignore sky position angles, and binning by projected separation preserves the model under a log-uniform semimajor-axis law. The archive contains the 21-page manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) with complete proofs, a Python library (likelihoods, observables, estimators, Kepler simulators), the full validation script with recorded results and figures, semantic negative controls, fast CI checks, the bounded novelty report and SHA-256 sums. All data are synthetic; no observational catalogue is analysed. Assurance boundary: written proofs; floating-point numerical checks and Kepler simulations; producer-side replay in normal and optimised modes; internal AI-assisted review (five roles, adversarial correctness review, proof audit and re-review). This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Prose, manuscript and data CC0-1.0; code MIT.

items.summary: Real Analysis Volume 1: Foundations of Real Analysis , authored by Helbert Justo Luque Zevallos and published by Proyecto Ágora as part of the Undergraduate Mathematics Series , is a university-level academic textbook devoted to the logical, algebraic, and axiomatic foundations of real analysis. The book provides a systematic and rigorous introduction to mathematical reasoning, formal proof techniques, and the fundamental structure of the real number system. Its primary objective is to develop the conceptual understanding and mathematical maturity required for advanced undergraduate studies in mathematical analysis. Chapter 1: Mathematical Language and Proof Techniques This chapter introduces propositional logic, logical connectives, truth tables, implications, equivalences, universal and existential quantifiers, and the negation of quantified statements. It develops the theory of sets, equivalence and order relations, injective, surjective, and bijective functions, images, preimages, composition, and inverse functions. Particular emphasis is placed on direct proof, proof by contraposition, proof by contradiction, mathematical induction, and the construction of counterexamples. The chapter also examines rigorous mathematical writing, common logical errors, finite and infinite sets, countability, and the uncountability of the real numbers. Chapter 2: The Real Number System The second chapter develops the axiomatic structure of the real numbers through field axioms, order axioms, and the compatibility of algebraic operations with order. It examines absolute value, the triangle inequality, fundamental inequalities, intervals, neighborhoods, upper and lower bounds, suprema, infima, maxima, and minima. A central component is the completeness property of the real numbers , including the structural distinction between rational and real numbers, the Archimedean property, the density of rational and irrational numbers, and the nested interval theorem. The chapter concludes with significant consequences of completeness, including the existence of roots, rational approximations, the supremum principle as a mathematical proof technique, and the relationship between completeness and convergence. Pedagogical Approach The textbook integrates precise definitions, propositions, lemmas, theorems, complete mathematical proofs, explanatory examples, and carefully constructed counterexamples. It includes 120 fully solved exercises and 150 proposed exercises , organized according to the main topics of the two chapters. These activities reinforce theoretical understanding, logical reasoning, mathematical writing, and independent problem-solving skills. Intended Audience This publication is intended for undergraduate mathematics students, university instructors, mathematics educators, and independent learners seeking a rigorous foundation in real analysis. As the first volume of a six-volume academic collection, it establishes the theoretical and methodological foundations for subsequent studies of sequences, numerical series, limits, continuity, metric spaces, compactness, differential calculus, Riemann integration, uniform convergence, and differential equations. items.summary: This record contains the source code, trained models, and derived research artifacts associated with the study “Physical fidelity and forecasting in compressed active matter representations.” The study evaluates how dimensionality reduction affects spatial reconstruction, physical fidelity, and temporal forecasting in active-matter simulations. It compares unconstrained, physics-constrained, realizability-constrained, and combined autoencoders with proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), at latent dimensions of 128, 256, and 512. Forecasting comparisons include linear autoregression, multilayer perceptrons, and persistence baselines. Reconstruction accuracy, physical admissibility, and forecast performance are treated as distinct evaluation objectives. The archive includes: • Source code for data acquisition, representation training, posthoc analysis, frozen final evaluation, and publication rendering. • Scientific configurations and dependency specifications. • Selected trained checkpoints, POD models, fitted forecasters, latent caches, training histories, and validation analyses. • Frozen final-test outputs, comparison summaries, coverage diagnostics, and provenance records. • Numerical visual exports, software tests, and workflow documentation. The original simulation data were downloaded from The Well, specifically its active_matter dataset. We acknowledge the original simulation contributors and the developers and curators of The Well. The original HDF5 simulation files are not redistributed in this record; the repository documents their acquisition, pinned revision, and content-hash verification. items.summary: We examine the role of the compact Lie group $SO(3)\times O(2)$ in the metric critical-point theory of normalized thick knots. The quotient by this group is part of the construction of ropelength-filtered knot spaces, but passage to an orbit space need not preserve the weak-slope notion of criticality. We establish elementary structural results for the action, including finiteness of isotropy for nontrivial knot types and exact invariance of the descending strong slope under a compact isometric quotient. We give counterexamples, including one with the connected group $SO(2)$, showing that the analogous assertion for the weak slope fails in general. On the other hand, we prove that it does hold, up to a multiplicative constant, at every point where the orbit map admits a Lipschitz local section together with a continuous gauge, and we construct such data for normalized thick knots from finitely many Fourier modes. items.summary: We examine the role of the compact Lie group $SO(3)\times O(2)$ in the metric critical-point theory of normalized thick knots. The quotient by this group is part of the construction of ropelength-filtered knot spaces, but passage to an orbit space need not preserve the weak-slope notion of criticality. We give counterexamples, including one with the connected group $SO(2)$, showing that the analogous assertion for the weak slope fails in general. On the other hand, we prove that it does hold, up to a multiplicative constant, at every point where the orbit map admits a Lipschitz local section together with a continuous gauge, and we construct such data for normalized thick knots from finitely many Fourier modes. For the unknot the round circles, whose isotropy is $O(2)$, remain outside this reduction. We also show that configurations whose thickness is not saturated have descending strong slope at least $2\pi/(\pi+1)$. items.summary: Real Analysis Volume 1: Foundations of Real Analysis , authored by Helbert Justo Luque Zevallos and published by Proyecto Ágora as part of the Undergraduate Mathematics Series , is a university-level academic textbook devoted to the logical, algebraic, and axiomatic foundations of real analysis. Its primary objective is to develop the conceptual understanding and mathematical maturity required for advanced undergraduate studies in mathematical analysis. It examines absolute value, the triangle inequality, fundamental inequalities, intervals, neighborhoods, upper and lower bounds, suprema, infima, maxima, and minima. A central component is the completeness property of the real numbers , including the structural distinction between rational and real numbers, the Archimedean property, the density of rational and irrational numbers, and the nested interval theorem. The chapter concludes with significant consequences of completeness, including the existence of roots, rational approximations, the supremum principle as a mathematical proof technique, and the relationship between completeness and convergence. items.summary: An institution's directives may in fact serve its recipients' reasons, as Raz's Normal Justification Thesis requires, while the institution lacks standing to insist that recipients forgo their own checks. This article separates objective authority from that entitlement. For continuing, consequential, and contestable directives, the entitlement depends on two substantiated presuppositions of the demand: that deference is worthwhile for the recipient's reference class, with a route for individual rebuttal, and that the exposure to error it creates is correctable at the scale of issuance. Given a justified directive role and a decision not reserved to the recipient's own judgment, the two are jointly sufficient. Serviceability is operationalized by a Scale-Indexed Serviceability test applied to a specified mechanism, lawful architecture, horizon, issuance scale, and claim mix. Failure to substantiate withholds the entitlement; a certified absence of any feasible plan defeats it and requires affected adverse issuance, or its effect, to be restricted to what can be serviced. Neither status invalidates lawful acts. Two consequences follow: a Wide-Scope Duty of Sustainable Issuance binds the bodies controlling scale and capacity, and Deontic Debt preserves directed claims when due obligations are deficiently serviced, even where incapacity is excused. A stipulated benefits administration shows each status at work. It reproduces the baseline waiting times and checks the defeat, withholding, and recovery scenarios. Python 3 standard library only; run with python3 halden_schedule_check.py . Related work. It accounts for dataset size and labels across classification, detection, and multi-dataset training. If profiling runs out of memory during backward computation, AutoBatch treats that as a limit rather than relying on an invalid measurement. 🛡️ Model YAML parsing is safer and more consistent. Activations must resolve to supported torch.nn modules, and model entries must be PyTorch module classes. Custom YAMLs using other expressions may need updating. 💾 Saving prediction results is more robust. Results.save() and plot(save=True) now produce sensible .jpg filenames for sources such as webcams, videos, or missing paths, and create parent directories when needed. 🔄 Similarity search uses the selected image directory on each startup. This avoids reusing stale indexes from another dataset; the trade-off is that embeddings are rebuilt each time. 🧩 Dataset and URL handling is more dependable. Non-PNG semantic masks are resolved before cache hashing, and URL schemes such as HTTPS:// , GS:// , and UL:// are now handled without case sensitivity. 📈 Benchmarking and evaluation guidance are clearer. TensorFlow GraphDef benchmarks now include OBB and pose, and the docs explain that classes absent from validation receive the overall mAP value rather than a measured per-class score. 🎯 Purpose & Impact ✅ AutoBatch is less likely to choose a batch size that exceeds a small dataset or available GPU memory, and multi-dataset World/YOLOE training avoids label-access failures. 🔒 Consistent, restricted YAML parsing improves safety, though nonstandard custom model configurations may no longer load. 🧰 More reliable result saving, mask-cache updates, and URL routing reduce common workflow errors. 🔍 Similarity search results better reflect the images currently in the chosen folder, while requiring index-building work at startup. 📚 Documentation updates clarify metric interpretation and integration behavior; no new model architecture is introduced in this release. items.summary: AnaTele is an open-source desktop tool for investigating ArduPilot flight logs (.tlog, .bin, .log). It infers flight phases, replays the recorded path in 3D, evaluates a versioned declarative rule pack with four explicit result states, and ranks competing failure hypotheses by capped evidence-family support minus contradictions, without assigning probabilities. items.summary: Phase-fixed weighted Gerchberg-Saxton (WGS) is the practical method for large arrays of optical traps, but it optimizes the hologram on an ideal model of the spatial light modulator (SLM), and the sequences that move traps interpolate between holograms that were never optimized for the frames in between. We test two hypotheses against the strongest baselines on the same scalar Fourier model. First, keeping the WGS weights but replacing the phase update by conjugate-gradient steps through the pixel-crosstalk kernel and the phase quantizer of the device (device-aware WGS) lowers the trap-intensity spread on the device. On a 10 x 10 lattice behind a crosstalk device, the relative standard deviation falls from a median of 5.21 percent for phase-fixed WGS at 30 iterations (5.21 percent at 100) to 0.205 percent, a median factor of 26 over 5 seeds (range 16 to 33) at a median 0.995 of the baseline's efficiency; the factor is 7.9 with 4-bit phase and a fill factor of 0.85 added, and 2.0 on a smaller 8 x 8 grid with flicker added and a fixed 30-iteration budget (the ratio of the means of 3 seeds); over the 5 geometries of the studio's benchmark on that device the median factor is 1.73 (0.97 to 4.69), and 2 of them meet both thresholds. A control that removes the device model from the loop gains nothing (5.14 percent), so the gain comes from the model. Second, optimizing every intermediate hologram of a moving-trap sequence with the trap phases locked to a smooth trajectory (flicker-bounded sequence) keeps the minimum transient intensity of the moving traps at a median 0.920 of their mean (range 0.915 to 0.932) over 5 seeds at 13 frames (below 0.9 at seven frames), against 0.654 (0.551 to 0.709) for linear phase interpolation. On longer moves, with the frames that keep the peak step per frame at most 0.2 Fourier units, the bound is met on 6 and 6 of 8 seeds of two lattice moves and on 5 of 6 seeds of a rearrangement case; the seeds that miss it miss it on the phase path their end phases prescribe, and at an equal number of frames on the rearrangement linear phase interpolation leads. Both results hold in a model of a simulated device and in a transient model that we define; neither is a hardware measurement. items.summary: Online sensor telemetry feeds the digital-twin, forecasting, control, and maintenance tools of instrumented water infrastructure. Probes deployed in these assets silently accumulate drift, flatlines, volatility bursts, and outages that existing pipelines often miss, because detectors and imputers are evaluated separately and under inflated synthetic metrics, and decay is treated as isolated events. This work proposes HARDIO, a Health-Aware Reliable Detection-Imputation Orchestrator, an operational data-quality framework that pairs a duration-weighted sensor decay scorecard with a per-variable, chained detector-imputer benchmark. The assignment is selected by a four-pillar composite score (operational 35%, health coverage 30%, reconstruction 20%, calibration 15%) that scores the signal an operator actually receives after detection and imputation. HARDIO processes sensor installations independently, enabling parallel execution and avoiding the need to evaluate all plant channels jointly. HARDIO is validated on the Cheles wastewater treatment plant (WWTP), a real 1,177 population-equivalent (PE) plant, over 432 days, 19 channels, and eight sensor installations. No single detector-imputer pair is best for every channel, so detection and chained imputation distribute across SAITS, KNN Residual, and LSTM-AE. Chained quality is reported for all 19 channels using 1-NRMSE; relative R² is interpreted on the 16 channels where the signal variance makes it meaningful, and 12 of these exceed R²=0.90. On the held-out final 20% of the record (12 channels in five installations), HARDIO achieves a mean chained 1-NRMSE of 0.976, within 0.0035 of a per-channel oracle, and outperforms the uniform SAITS pipeline (p=0.003). Its reconstruction performance is close to that of the strongest uniform pipelines, without a statistically significant improvement over them, and slightly below that of a single detector-imputer pair selected on validation data (0.978). The released artefact exposes the model map, confidence labels, margins, and production masks for decision support.
items.title: Experimental Artefacts for HARDIO: A Health-Aware Reliable Detection-Imputation Orchestrator for Operational Data Quality in Instrumented Water Infrastructure

items.summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . items.summary: Coarse flood maps support regional risk assessment but omit terrain detail relevant to local exposure. We present floodsr, a Python framework for reconstructing fine-grid flood depths using a trained residual U-Net (ResUNet) or the existing terrain-based CostGrow method. We trained the terrain-conditioned ResUNet on paired Canadian hydraulic simulations and evaluated it on withheld spatial tiles and independent simulations at two external sites. Wet-loss training improved reconstruction on five selected tiles, although internal validation favoured the deployed baseline. External depth errors decreased, but wet-depth errors and spatial agreement did not improve consistently. CPU benchmarks quantified runtime and memory for both methods, and repeatability and input-validation checks passed in the tested configurations. The framework supports comparison and reuse of reconstruction methods; application-specific validation remains necessary because finer grids do not guarantee more accurate flood maps.   Non-peer-reviewed preprint. items.summary: Software built for elderly care is usually described rather than measured. This paper reports an instrumented measurement of CareCompanion, a working Android application that presents two distinct interface surfaces over one data model: an enlarged, photograph-first surface for the cared-for person and a dense administration console for the family member who manages their care. Five instruments were run against one frozen commit on a single day: the automated test suite three times over (441 test executions), 120 timed HTTPS requests across 4 backend endpoints, 51 anonymous read attempts against all 17 database tables, a complete census of 302 declared interface sizes, and the release artefact. The strongest results are a median care-data read latency of 128 ms (95th percentile 440 ms, n = 30); an elder-surface median control of 64 dp against the 48 dp platform minimum, 1.3× that floor; a median elder type size of 20 sp against 13 sp on the guardian surface; and zero rows of personal data returned to an unauthenticated reader holding the application's own key, across all 13 personal tables. Set against the literature, the elder surface exceeds the published geometry it was designed from, the latency sits an order of magnitude inside the one-second interaction threshold, and the data isolation is materially better than the audited baseline for deployed health applications. Two results go the other way and are reported as measured: the guardian surface is below the platform's interactive minimum at the median, and 17 % of elder text is declared below 16 sp. No health outcome is claimed.
items.title: Measuring a Dual-Surface Elder-Care Android Application: Interface Geometry, Latency and Data Isolation

items.summary: An institution's directives may in fact serve its recipients' reasons, as Raz's Normal Justification Thesis requires, while the institution lacks standing to insist that recipients forgo their own checks. For continuing, consequential, and contestable directives, the entitlement depends on two substantiated presuppositions of the demand: that deference is worthwhile for the recipient's reference class, with a route for individual rebuttal, and that the exposure to error it creates is correctable at the scale of issuance. Given a justified directive role and a decision not reserved to the recipient's own judgment, the two are jointly sufficient. Serviceability is operationalized by a Scale-Indexed Serviceability test applied to a specified mechanism, lawful architecture, horizon, issuance scale, and claim mix. Failure to substantiate withholds the entitlement; a certified absence of any feasible plan defeats it and requires affected adverse issuance, or its effect, to be restricted to what can be serviced. Neither status invalidates lawful acts. Two consequences follow: a Wide-Scope Duty of Sustainable Issuance binds the bodies controlling scale and capacity, and Deontic Debt preserves directed claims when due obligations are deficiently serviced, even where incapacity is excused. A stipulated benefits administration shows each status at work. items.summary: This record contains the supporting materials of the article “A trade-based Forest Club as a path to halting tropical deforestation”. It has two parts: a multi-regional input–output (MRIO) assessment of the deforestation embodied in agricultural trade and consumption, and the computable general equilibrium (CGE) model of the Forest Club . Every figure and table of the article, its Extended Data and its Supplementary Information is produced from the code, input data and results provided here. The Forest Club is a trade-based coalition. Its members hold their forest at its 2019 extent and are deemed compliant with the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR). They charge the forest-risk commodities they import from non-members, either with a flat penalty or with a surcharge proportional to the deforestation embodied in each product. 1. MRIO impact assessment (folders 1. Data and 2. MRIO) The forest-to-cropland and forest-to-pasture transitions of HILDA+ v2.1 (2012–2019) are extracted from the netCDF files and assigned to countries. They are then allocated to the agricultural sectors of the GLORIA MRIO using FAOSTAT harvested areas and livestock numbers, smoothed with three-year moving averages; the FAO–GLORIA mapping and the hectares per head are in A-1_FAO_Cropland_mapping_GLORIA.xlsx and A-2_Head_per_ha.xlsx. Consumption-based accounting (CBA) attributes this agricultural deforestation to final consumers. Throughflow-based accounting (TBA, by hypothetical extraction) traces the share that transits through intermediary economies such as the EU, in detail for Brazil, Indonesia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The folders hold the Python script (CBA_TBA_script.py), the Alteryx workflows, the satellite accounts, the results and the visualisation files (Tableau, Sankey diagrams). These produce sections 2–4 of the Supplementary Information (Tables S1–S2, Figs S1–S4), which describe the deforestation the EUDR covers. 2. CGE model (synced from GitHub) The study simulates how the club forms, round by round, as each country compares its welfare inside and outside it. The model is GTAP-AEZ, a global CGE model with agro-ecological zones (42 regions, 35 sectors, 18 zones; GEMPACK). Every result is measured against a baseline that combines the EUDR with the business-as-usual clearing that DeDuCE v2.1 attributes to agriculture. The coalitions reached are tested for one-country deviations and for their sensitivity to the switching cost. 0_External_data: footprint intensities and border charges derived from DeDuCE v2.1, the EUDR import cut shares, the business-as-usual clearing by region and agro-ecological zone (HILDA+ v2.1 patterns; MapBiomas RAD 2025 for Brazil), and the productivity calibration of the cleared land. 1_Code: R scripts that calibrate and solve the two-stage baseline, run the membership game and the one-deviation stability tests, and calibrate the land-supply elasticities to Miranda et al. (2024). 2_Model: the GTAP-AEZ model files (TABLO code, command files, sets and aggregation). 3_Output and 4_DB: the text outputs of every solve and the result tables of every run, by region and round, for all membership processes and stability tests of the paper. 5_Figures: the Python pipeline that redraws all figures and tables from these results, with their source data. Data not included The GTAP Data Base (version 12, reference year 2019) is licensed by the Center for Global Trade Analysis, Purdue University. items.summary: Physical reservoir computing leverages the rich dynamical response of non-linear physical bodies to process temporal information without electronic microprocessors. Tensegrity structures, networks of discontinuous compression struts suspended within continuous tension cables, exhibit exceptional compliance, multi-stability, and high-dimensional configuration manifolds, making them prime candidates for mechanical intelligence in extreme, radiation-heavy environments. However, current methodologies rely predominantly on heuristic evolutionary algorithms or brute-force trial-and-error to configure such systems, lacking a rigorous analytical design framework. In this paper, we bridge this gap by establishing an explicit, first-principles mathematical mapping between the internal self-stress null space of a tensegrity network and its Information Processing Capacity (IPC). By decomposing the tangent stiffness matrix into material elastic ($K_e$) and pre-stress geometric ($K_g$) contributions, we demonstrate that the computational memory and fading-memory time constants of a tensegrity reservoir can be systematically engineered by tuning member pre-tensions within an admissible convex cone, holding spatial geometry strictly constant.
items.title: Formally Verified Pre-Stress Manifolds for Dynamic Stability and Adaptive Physical Intelligence in Tensegrity Reservoir Computing

items.summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A wide binary star takes thousands of years to complete one orbit, so its eccentricity usually cannot be found by following the orbit. Astronomers instead use the angle Γ between the pair's projected separation and projected relative velocity, whose distribution over many binaries depends on the population's eccentricity law. Hwang, Ting and Zakamska (MNRAS 2022, Appendix B) asked whether this angle distribution determines the eccentricity distribution uniquely. In the ideal model (random orbital phase, uniformly random 3D orientation, error-free projections) this package derives the likelihood of one angle in closed form, p(γ|e) = [acosh(1/e) − 1{|cos γ| > e} acosh(|cos γ|/e)] / (π sin²γ), and shows that its mixtures are classical Abel transforms. This gives an explicit inverse for every eccentricity law, including atoms: different eccentricity laws never give the same angle law. The inverse is continuous in the weak topology but discontinuous in total variation, so fine structure can be nearly invisible. Moments need no inversion: E√(1−e²) = (π/2) E sin³Γ and E e² = 1/2 + E cos 2Γ − (1/2) E cos 4Γ; these are the only symmetric unbiased single-angle observables for their targets and give near-efficient power-law index estimators. Two exact selection results bear on Gaia samples: thermal populations keep a uniform angle law under selections that ignore sky position angles, and binning by projected separation preserves the model under a log-uniform semimajor-axis law. The archive contains the 21-page manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) with complete proofs, a Python library (likelihoods, observables, estimators, Kepler simulators), the full validation script with recorded results and figures, semantic negative controls, fast CI checks, the bounded novelty report and SHA-256 sums. All data are synthetic; no observational catalogue is analysed. items.summary: CIRCULAR MATERIAL ECONOMIES FOR AUTONOMOUS MOBILE CITIES AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:移動城市循環經濟與材料永續極限 55/90 CIRCULAR MATERIAL ECONOMIES FOR AUTONOMOUS MOBILE CITIES AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 55 of 90). It investigates whether a deliberately unoccupied six-module mobile-city research system can reduce relocation-related material loss through qualified reuse, automated selective disassembly and auditable remanufacturing, while preserving deployment latency and critical-service safety. The three-way research coupling is Circular Materials x Autonomous Manufacturing x Urban Sustainability. Neither a functioning autonomous city nor a human-occupied habitat is asserted. The falsifiable proposal compares a frozen circular material strategy against competent conventional manual recovery, replacement and stationary emergency infrastructure under equal material, energy, sensing, technician-hour, tool, water and transport budgets. Original intake, declined parts, work in progress, consumed adhesives, repeated repairs, rejected batches and retired material remain in the denominator. Blind faults include grade swaps, hidden fatigue, wrong material passports, replayed scale measurements, contamination, source-energy omissions and optimistic virgin-substitution credits. A proposal fails whenever a load-bearing component, utility service, waste route, safety interlock or material identity cannot be independently reconstructed. Thirty mechanism-distinct research formula plates address mass custody, qualified yield, bond separation work, fatigue, polymer rheology, sensor residuals, covariance, electrical energy, verified lifecycle inventory, carbon-allocation sensitivity, replacement counterfactuals, tail risk, second-site reproduction and noncompensatory physical release. The original contract's cyber-physical residual r_k = y_k - yhat_k(x_k,u_k) is retained as one fault-detection method; it is not treated as a law of circularity or sustainability. Every mathematical plate states units, validity assumptions, a blinded counterexample and scientific chapter interfaces. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated research studies and 200 Research Gates, each connected to a specified material state, independent reference, fault or competing process. Thirty-three different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose research instruments, material-qualification fixtures, provenance devices, circularity accounting tools and successor-ready evidence protocols. This work proposes hypotheses and reproducibility obligations, not physical trial outcomes. Its complete PDF also contains research limits, negative-result custody and second-laboratory transfer requirements. The scope remains prospective, scaled and non-occupancy. Environmental performance requires functional-unit parity and a complete lifecycle inventory; increasing recovered mass alone does not prove lower environmental burden. Relevant method references include Ostapska et al. (10.1016/j.spc.2024.05.014), Formentini et al. (10.1016/j.jclepro.2025.145459), Attia et al. (10.1016/j.autcon.2024.105521), Mao and Cao (10.1016/j.spc.2024.12.021), Poschmann et al. (10.1002/cite.201900107) and Keating et al. (10.1126/scirobotics.aam8986). The Flagship 13 mother genealogy identifiers (10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839) were provided by the author and their metadata have not been independently confirmed. No external study cited here establishes this integrated F55 architecture.
